newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Aleman calls for land occupations end.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Aleman calls for land occupations end.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Monday called on Nicaraguans to stop illegally occupying land they do not own as the government tries to resolve its lingering problems with private property.

Nicaragua's dominant political forces, Aleman's right-wing Liberal Alliance and the left-wing Sandinista Front, have initiated a series of meetings to find a solution to the property problem, left over from the 1979-1990 Sandinista government when the state confiscated private property.

Despite attempts to resolve the issue, conflicts between the current and former occupants are still a source of social unrest and uncertainty over property laws has led poor families to continue occupying other people's homes.
Sandinista leaders charged that police carried out a wave of violent evictions after the right-wing government was inaugurated on Jan. 10 and called on the government to halt the evictions.

But Aleman on Monday told reporters owners have the right to go to court to recover their property and said the illegal occupations were scaring investors away from Nicaragua. "For this reason I call on the citizenry to not invade land to avoid their eviction by the National Police," he said.
In a flurry of legislation before leaving office after their 1990 election loss, the Sandinistas awarded themselves more than 200,000 properties they had confiscated.

Aleman said his government would give legal titles to the thousands of poor families who received confiscated properties while compensating the former owners. But it will make wealthy Sandinistas who got confiscated land return it or pay for it, threatening to set off conflicts with powerful Sandinistas.
The next meeting between the Sandinista and Liberal property commissions is on Feb. 6.
